claims: The United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) is the primary federal law enforcement arm of the U.S. Postal Service.
USPIS protects the mail system, employees, and customers.
USPIS investigates over 200 mail-related federal crimes.
Postal Inspectors are armed federal agents.
Postal Inspectors combat mail theft, fraud, dangerous mail, and identity theft.
Postal Inspectors ensure the integrity of the nation's 30,000+ postal facilities.
USPIS investigates the theft of mail, mail fraud, prohibited mailings (drugs, explosives), and dangerous mail.
USPIS protects postal employees and customers from violence and threats, including robberies.
Postal Inspectors have authority to serve warrants, subpoenas, and make arrests for postal-related crimes.
USPIS protects the infrastructure, revenue, and assets of the U.S. Postal Service.
USPIS is the oldest federal law enforcement agency in the U.S.
USPIS utilizes Postal Police Officers besides Postal Inspectors.
Postal Police Officers secure high-value facilities and assets.
USPIS has inspectors in every state to support investigations.
